summary: The core is a compact behavioral re-implementation split into generic MAIN/VIDEO/SOUND blocks. It has no Konami 005849 module, no board net names and no board raster timing. Its video runs as a scan-time pipeline, but every FPGA core without a frame buffer needs one, and the pipeline's semantics follow MAME's tilemap/sprite description (48-sprite loop, y!=0 skip, sx - 2*(attr&0x80), BG category drawn over sprites). The interrupt generator uses a software bit trick (~tick & (tick+1)) on a free-running tick counter seeded with per-title fudge values, not the chip's V-counter decode. The sprite-bank polarity also matches MAME's own self-described wrong-way mapping. Taken together the code reads as written from emulator behavior, not from the board.

findings.note: The board's 005849 video/interrupt controller has no module of its own and no chip pins. Its jobs are spread over a VIDEO module (tile scan, sprite scan, mixer, palette) and an IRQGEN inside MAIN. The split is by function (CPU side / video / sound), not by PCB parts.

findings.signal: Interrupt generator uses C bit-trick on free-running tick counter
findings.note: A 9-bit 'tick' advances every 16 lines, and interrupts fire on irqs = (~tick)&(tick+1), a software idiom that isolates the bits going 0->1. Bit 0 drives NMI (every 32 lines) and bits 3/4 drive IRQ/FIRQ. This reproduces MAME's rates (NMI 8x/frame, FIRQ every other frame) through an abstract counter, not through raster-counter decode. On reset the tick is seeded with per-title constants (24/48), which no hardware mechanism explains.

findings.signal: Interrupt ack mirrors MAME's enable-bit-clears-line semantics
findings.note: A write to E044 latches mask bits 0-2, and a 0 in an enable bit clears the matching line. That is MAME's ctrl_w model of register 4. IRQ and FIRQ are merged onto one Z80 INT, like MAME's input_merger in gberet_state::gberet.

findings.signal: Sprite RAM bank polarity matches MAME's acknowledged-wrong mapping
findings.mame_ref: gberet.cpp: gberet_state::draw_sprites (ctrl_r(3)&0x08 selects spriteram2 at d000) and header TODO
findings.note: SPRB <= ~CPUWD[3], so with bit 3 set the engine reads offset 0x000 (D000). That reproduces MAME's selection, which MAME's own TODO says is reversed from the real chip. The core follows the emulator's behavior, not the chip register's definition.

findings.signal: Sprite engine reproduces draw_sprites loop semantics
findings.note: The engine walks sprite entries 0..0x2F (`define SPRITES 8'h30 = 0xc0/4) in RAM order and skips entries with y==0 (py!=0, as in MAME's if (sr[offs+3])). It computes px = sat2 - {sat1[7],8'h0} (MAME's sr[2] - 2*(attr&0x80)) and code = {attr[6],sr[0]}. Later sprites overwrite earlier ones in the line buffer, which keeps MAME's draw order. The per-line scan itself is ordinary FPGA line-buffer engineering.

findings.signal: Scan-time BG pipeline driven by H/V position
findings.note: Tile addresses, row-scroll lookup (ZRMA = BGVP[7:3]), flip XOR and CLUT PROM lookup all come from the pixel counters each pixel. That is scan-time, but the layout (64x32 rows, 32 scroll rows, code = vram + attr bit6<<8, flips from attr[5:4], category attr[7]) is the same data MAME's tilemap holds, and the offsets (+16, +8) are just alignment.

findings.signal: Per-pixel priority mux and PROM-addressed palette
findings.note: One combinational mux picks BG-high, then sprite, then BG for each pixel and feeds a 5-bit palette PROM address ({1,BGPT} for tiles, {0,SPPT} for sprites). This is how the board produces MAME's three-pass draw, and the raw PROM byte goes straight to RGB with no resistor-weight table. It is weak evidence, since any line-buffer core would do the same.

findings.signal: Full-address equality decode following the memory map
findings.note: Each port and RAM is chip-selected by exact 16-bit compares (e.g. CPUAD==16'hF603, ==16'hE043) taken from the address map, with no partial 74LS138-style decode or mirroring. The addresses themselves are neutral, but the decode style is an address map, not board logic. Unmapped reads return 0 instead of open bus.

The raster is 396x256 from a 48 MHz/8 clock with an 8-bit V counter, against the board's 384x264 at 6.144 MHz. No 005849 H/V counter bits drive fetch phases. The timing is built for the video output, not copied from the PCB.
Data is latched at F200 and written to the SN76489 on an F400 access. MAME and the board share this behavior. The fractional clock divider is FPGA engineering.

findings.where: rtl/GreenBeret_VIDEO.v (no flip-screen or edge-column mask); rtl/FPGA_GreenBeret.v:84-87 (PALD/CPUD tied 0)
findings.mame_ref: k005849.cpp: ctrl reg 3 bit7, reg 4 bit3
findings.note: Flip screen, the 005849 edge-column mask and the coin counters are not implemented. The core adds no behavior that MAME lacks (no bus contention, no wait states, no open bus).
